iWant: to set Squire up on my Mac from one download, one step at a time, without ever opening Terminal
soThat: I can install and start using my own assistant without technical help
description: The installer journey: the Mac check, one yes for what will be installed, Apple's developer tools, Claude Code, the Claude sign-in, naming the Squire, the folders, the always-on session, the phone, the Keychain, the browser, the nightly backup, wake-ups, voice notes, the health check and the guided first conversation. The installer also sets Claude Code's auto-compact window. The eligibility refusal (a Mac below macOS 13, or a Claude plan below Pro) is part of this journey and is defined at this journey's round.
title: Set-up: from the download to a first reply, with no Terminal

acceptanceCriteria.description: Setting Squire up never needs Terminal.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A fresh macOS user on a Mac that meets Squire's requirements
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire is set up from the download to the end of set-up
acceptanceCriteria.then: Set-up completes with no Terminal window opened by or for the Squire owner.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The installer sets Claude Code's auto-compact window to 500k tokens, and the health check reports any drift from it.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A fresh Claude Code configuration for Squire's session, configurations that set the auto-compact window otherwise by the routes that reach that session (its config folder's settings, at the top level and per model; the environment Squire's runner gives it; the Mac's managed settings file and managed preferences), and the routes that do not reach it (the Squire owner's own Claude Code settings, environment and command line)
acceptanceCriteria.when: The installer runs and Squire's session starts, and a setting later changes the window
acceptanceCriteria.then: The session's effective auto-compact window is 500k tokens after the installer runs, and the health check reports the drift when a setting changes it.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Setting Squire up and using it for the first time work end to end on a fresh Mac.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A fresh macOS user on a Mac that meets Squire's requirements, with a Claude Pro plan or above
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Squire owner runs the installer from the download and opens their Squire
acceptanceCriteria.then: Every step passes without Terminal, and the Squire owner gets a first reply from their Squire.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When set-up meets a problem, Squire explains it, keeps what is done and the Squire owner's things, and carries on or resumes without starting again.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Set-up on a Mac where something goes wrong: macOS older than Squire needs, a Mac that cannot install Apple's tools for this user, a Claude plan the Squire owner says is below Pro, or a plan found below Pro at sign-in; a download that fails, times out or is interrupted, or a second install started over a first; a sign-in that is cancelled, times out or has no internet; no phone to hand, or the laptop closed during the first conversation
acceptanceCriteria.then: An unsupported macOS, or a plan the Squire owner says is below Pro, stops set-up before it changes anything on the Mac. A plan found below Pro at sign-in stops set-up and leaves the Mac as set-up found it. Either way, Squire explains what is missing and the way on. A failed, timed-out or interrupted download, or a second install over a first, leaves no half-finished installation, keeps the Squire owner's data and settings, and resumes or repairs the one installation. A cancelled, timed-out or offline sign-in is explained, keeps the progress made and resumes without reinstalling. With no phone, or with the laptop closed during the first conversation, the Mac set-up still completes, the first conversation resumes where it stopped, and the phone can join later.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When a source that could change Squire's compaction window cannot be read, the health check says it cannot confirm the window.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Squire set up, and a source that could set the session's auto-compact window which exists but cannot be read: the Mac's managed settings file or folder, or its managed preferences for Claude Code
acceptanceCriteria.then: The health check says it cannot confirm the compaction window and names the source it could not read; it never reports the window as confirmed and never stays silent.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A set-up step whose result Squire cannot confirm is run again from its start and is never counted as done.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Set-up on a Mac where the result of a step cannot be confirmed: Claude Code's launcher is present but the version it points to is incomplete, or Apple's tools still report that they are installing
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire's set-up reaches that step, or is run again after it
acceptanceCriteria.then: Squire runs the step again from its start and does not record it as done until its result is confirmed; a later run never skips it.

acceptanceCriteria.description: When set-up cannot read a fact about the Mac it needs, it refuses before changing anything, saying what it could not read and the way on.
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Mac whose facts set-up must read cannot be read: its macOS version reading is missing, fails or is not a version, its memory reading is missing, fails or is not a whole number, or, with Apple's tools absent, the list of the user's groups cannot be read
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Squire owner opens Squire's download
acceptanceCriteria.then: Set-up refuses before it changes anything on the Mac, names what it could not read and the way on, and never asks the owner for that fact or assumes it.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Before Squire's Claude sign-in ends, Squire warns its owner and, on the owner's yes, signs in again with no Terminal.
acceptanceCriteria.given: Squire set up, with its Claude sign-in due to end within seven days, and the day it ends readable without touching the sign-in's secret
acceptanceCriteria.when: Squire's background run checks the sign-in, and the Squire owner says yes to signing in again
acceptanceCriteria.then: Squire tells the owner through its own session, at most once a day, the day the sign-in ends and the one action to take; on the owner's yes it runs the sign-in again into Squire's own Claude Code configuration, opening the browser's sign-in page, with no Terminal and nothing else.
